summary.intent: Plan Phase 69 (FUSE/WinFsp Rust integration + grant-root awareness) via the GSD workflow, then auto-advance into wave-based parallel execution of the resulting plans.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (grew from 14 to 18 plans across three re-scopes); execution merged 12-13/18 plans (full crates/core + crates/sdk foundation, plus additive write-plane/read-adapter infra). The core FUSE cutover plan (69-09) required a multi-slice 'grind' after repeated architectural blockers; by session end crates/fuse library compiles green on node/v3 but tests, desktop wiring, and the SC#6 CI gate remain, with a live E2E merge gate still pending before combining with 69-18 and merging.

repo: gsd commit helper reports false-negative 'commit_failed' even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.
Worktree executors sometimes mis-report `expected_base` as their own last docs commit rather than the true fork base — verify with `git merge-base worktree-agent-<id> HEAD` before recording/merging.
`cargo fmt` on a crate's lib.rs follows `mod` declarations and can reformat the whole crate — scope-check diffs and revert out-of-scope reformats before committing.

InodeKind in crates/fuse is a read-WRITE vault-owner struct (holds ipns_private_key to sign IPNS records), unlike the web's read-only 68.2 model — any Rust read-path port must also materialize write keys, not just read keys.

ResolvedChild/list_folder (crates/sdk/src/listing.rs) is a keyless read-only projection; a separate ResolvedOwnedChild/list_folder_owned API was needed to recover write-plane keys for an existing tree.

Research-cited 'JournalOp weld' (parent_metadata: FolderMetadata in queue.rs) was stale/nonexistent by execution time — always re-verify research findings via live grep against the current tree before treating them as constraints.
SC#6 sanctioned read entrypoints: list_folder / list_shared_folder / list_folder_owned / fetch_node_gated; resolve_published_node must stay pub(crate).
D-07 dual-keying pairs read/write child refs by node identity (published.id == WriteChildRef.child_id), never by ipnsName.
Terminal-owner zeroization is enforced by the type system: parent_read_key is passed by borrow (&[u8]), so it cannot be zeroed by the callee.
RotationHighWater needed #[derive(Clone)] added (safe since JsonSidecarFloorStore just holds a PathBuf doing read-modify-write) to support spawned async tasks needing an owned copy.
NodeContent.file_iv is hex-encoded (not base64) — content_ops.rs uses hex::decode.
~250 legacy-model FUSE crypto unit tests became obsolete after the node/v3 migration; team decided to delete legacy tests and rely on live E2E rather than blind-rewrite them (risk of false-green).

crates/fuse/Cargo.toml default=["fuse"] with platform/windows/* behind cfg(feature="winfsp") means default `cargo check --workspace` never validates Windows code — only the cargo-windows CI lane does.

code.finding: InodeKind enum reshaped in Slice 1 of the 69-09 grind to Root/Folder/File variants each carrying read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key (all non-Option Zeroizing types), dropping legacy encrypted_folder_key/folder_key/file_meta_ipns_name/versions fields.

list_folder_owned added (Slice/plan 69-17) to materialize per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key} for an existing tree through the same anti-rollback gate as list_folder; fetch_node_gated added later for single-node gated fetch.

JournalOp reshaped (plan 69-18) from hex-string ECIES-under-user-key fields to child_published_node/parent_child_ref/parent_write_child_ref node/v3 fields; sdk-green but leaves crates/fuse workspace-red until 69-09 migrates consumers.

Legacy decrypt_journal_name helper (ECIES-unwrap of encrypted journal name) was deleted entirely rather than converted — the display name now travels inside the symmetric-sealed SealedChildRef.name field.

workflow: When a worktree-isolated executor's atomic plan can't compile-check as a whole, break it into bounded 'slices' each landing its own commit on the same branch, with a committed runbook capturing the target shape and carry-forward facts — this let the grind survive session/usage-limit interruptions without losing progress.

Before merging worktree work, independently verify a sub-agent's architectural-blocker claims (grep for the cited symbols/patterns yourself) rather than trusting the report at face value — this caught that one 'landmine' was stale and confirmed two other blockers were real.
For large, unverifiable-in-isolation crypto migrations, prefer a live end-to-end test gate over compile-green as the merge criterion, and say so explicitly rather than merging on cargo check alone.
When a durable handoff/scratchpad path is mistyped, fix it immediately with an explicit move rather than leaving two divergent copies.

friction: Initial gsd-planner sub-agent crashed mid-response (API connection closed), leaving 13/14 plans on disk — required filesystem-fallback recovery via a fresh single-plan planner.

Two later executor agents also died from API/session issues: one stalled mid-stream on a cosmetic edit (69-16) requiring manual finish-and-commit, another hit an account session limit mid-exploration (69-09) requiring a wait-and-retry.

Three successive in-execution architectural discoveries on the FUSE cutover (69-09): (1) read-swap not separable from write-path migration, (2) the Node write-plane emit API and read adapter didn't exist at all, (3) InodeKind is a read-write owner needing write-key materialization that the first two re-scopes still hadn't built — each required research+planning+approval cycles before execution could resume.
Scope was massively underestimated repeatedly: 69-09 was framed as a 'mechanical flip' but turned out to be a >1000-site, ~12,300 LOC crypto-model rewrite requiring a 5-slice grind.
gsd commit helper's false-negative 'commit_failed' report recurred on nearly every commit in the session, requiring manual git log verification each time.
A scratchpad handoff path was written with a doubled directory segment on first attempt, requiring a corrective move.
open_items: Slice 5c of the 69-09 grind: add SC#6 CI grep gate (must allowlist/wrap metadata.rs's bin-entry-publish and file-meta-reencrypt raw resolves), migrate/delete ~149 remaining fuse test-compile errors, and finish desktop wiring (mod.rs/prepopulate.rs, replay_for_vault caller signature, windows/* cfg-gated code).
Legacy FUSE test module (~250 tests, ~149 remaining after partial cleanup) needs legacy-model tests deleted and non-crypto mechanics/node-v3 fake-fetcher smoke tests added.

Before merging the combined 69-18+69-09 unit, must run a live local sdk-e2e + desktop-e2e (docker+TEE) pass, not just cargo check — flagged E2E risks: file `versions` not reconstructed on write (regression), file_iv hex round-trip correctness, orphaned IPFS pins not unpinned after replay re-publish (GC-able, non-blocking).

After 69-09 lands: still need 69-10 (delete legacy crates/core types), 69-13 (grant-gated write path + SC#2 + D-07), and 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows + TEST-03) which is autonomous:false and hands off to the user's Windows machine.
Phase 69 grew from the original 14 planned plans to 18 (69-15 through 69-18 added mid-execution) — ROADMAP/plan count bookkeeping should be double-checked for consistency once the phase closes.
